newsitem.title: RUSSIA: British woman gets new trial on Russia drug charge.
newsitem.headline: British woman gets new trial on Russia drug charge.

text.p: A Russian court will reopen the case of a British teenager, sentenced to six years in a labour camp last year for smuggling 4.6 kg (10 lb) of cocaine into Russia, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.
Tass quoted lawyers for 19-year-old Karen Henderson as saying the proceedings in the original trial had been poorly translated and Henderson had incriminated herself with some of her answers.
A new hearing would be held in front of different judges, but no date had yet been set, Tass said.
Henderson, from Scotland, was arrested in February 1996 at Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport.
She was flying from Havana to Warsaw via Moscow with a Dutch woman, who pleaded guilty to smuggling cocaine and is serving a six-year term.

Henderson pleaded not guilty at the original trial last October, saying she bought her suitcase from a man at the Havana airport without knowing that it contained drugs. She may also seek a pardon from President Boris Yeltsin.
